items.title: [GSoC] Pedestrian area routing: Build area polygons and generate medial axis
items.body: Continuation of #6127 ## What is this PR about Enables pedestrian routing through pedestrian areas (`highway=pedestrian` + `area=yes`). For each area it generates a traversal skeleton along the medial axis and connects the area's entrances to it, so a pedestrian can cross a square directly. ## Implementation - `ParseAreaWays`: areas tagged only on the relation have member ways with no routable tags, so lua drops them during regular way parsing. This pass recovers the ways referenced by area relations and marks them so their geometry survives to the builder. - `BuildAreas`: assembles each area's polygon/s from its member ways (including inner members), computes the medial axis via a Voronoi diagram of the densified boundary, prunes branches, connects each entrance to the nearest skeleton vertex it can reach without leaving the polygon, and materialises the result as synthetic footways. ConstructEdges then turns those into edges like any other way. - `Synthetic ids`: generated ways and nodes get ids above the highest real way and node ids, so they never collide with real OSM ids, and are kept out of the final tiles. ## Decisions we made - Areas below a size threshold keep their routable perimeter instead of a traversal. - Entrances within a few meters that can see each other through the area are merged, to avoid redundant connections. - Areas that already have pedestrian paths mapped inside are left untouched. - Densify tolerance at 4m, a speed/detail trade-off validated visually. ## Performance BuildAreas on Germany started at ~114s. With GEOSPrepare on the Voronoi filter and the two-pass node collection it dropped to ~65s, and raising the densify tolerance takes it further: 2m -> ~33s 4m -> ~19s Roughly 6 minutes projected for a full Europe build. ## Notes This is a fully functional version that we've tested on real data (Germany and Europe builds) with really good results. We've marked a number of TODOs in the code for things that work well but could be improved further down the line. Here's a before/after from [Plaza de Santo Domingo](https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/1525621) in Murcia, Spain, without the feature the route goes around the square, with it it crosses straight through: **Before**: **After**: ## A note on stability This is a functional first version. It works well and noticeably improves routing across pedestrian areas, though there are still things that could be refined and improved further down the line (marked as TODOs in the code). None of that affects existing behaviour: the whole feature sits behind the `mjolnir.pedestrian_areas` config option and is off by default, so unless it's explicitly enabled Valhalla builds and routes exactly as it does today.

items.title: Handling different types of pedestrian crossings
items.body:
OSM has widely used tags for annotating pedestrian (and/or bike) crossings, both on ways as well as on nodes. Valhalla currently only seems to care about ways tagged with `highway=crossing`, but does not distinguish between e.g. [zebra](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:crossing=zebra), [pelican](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:crossing_ref=pelican) or [unmarked](https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Tag:crossing%3Dunmarked) crossings. 

I think these could be used to improve path finding: e.g. as a pedestrian I would expect unmarked crossings to be penalized more compared to safer ones. 

Since representing crossings as either ways or as nodes are both common practices in OSM, this is not something easily solved... we would have to try handling both cases equally, and we would have to see if there is enough space on our data structures for it.

items.title: Pedestrians appear unable to leave sidewalks, rendering pedestrian routing in cities poorly supported
items.body:
In OpenStreetMap data, sidewalks are typically drawn separate from the road, even if there is no kerb in between. Thus, when routing, there is no physical connection to the road and walkers are routed all the way around any physical connection.
The concept of 'crossing a road', leaving a sidewalk, does not exist. That makes pedestrian routing in a city with many sidewalks poorly supported and comes with odd detours.
Google Maps appears not to draw sidewalks as such, avoiding the issue. But once they are properly drawn, then routing software should understand how walkers walk on them and how road crossings work.

See screenshot for a typical example. The footpath is adjacent to the local road, as usual. If there are no sideways at the same side of the road, the detour can be infinite. Just as long as it takes to have that physical (in OSM terms) connection.

![Screenshot 2023-11-29 at 9 48 11 am](https://github.com/valhalla/valhalla/assets/7885507/5cf211da-bc22-46ff-bf57-4aeedf0ba080)

items.title: [GSoC] Pedestrian area routing: Detect areas during parsing
items.body:
## Background

First step toward area routing is to detect pedestrian areas (`highway=pedestrian` and `area=yes`) during tile building, both as ways and multipolygon relations.

## Changes I have made

- lua/graph.lua: Ways and multipolygon relations of pedestrian areas were discarded, I have added support for them.
- valhalla/mjolnir/osmway.h: Add an area_ bit to mark pedestrian ways
- valhalla/mjolnir/osmdata.h: I have built an OSMArea struct and area_relations multimap indexed by relation id so we can see all members of the same relation
- src/mjolnir/graphbuilder.cc: skip area ways so it won't generate edges for them, which makes all the tests pass
- src/mjolnir/pbfgraphparser.cc: tag handler for simple ways + relation function for multipolygon areas, which collects outer/inner ways of the areas
- src/mjolnir/osmdata.cc: serialize/deserialize area_relations to a binary temp file between build stages
- scripts/valhalla_build_config: add mjolnir.pedestrian_areas boolean option (default false) so existing behavior is unchanged
- test/gurka/test_area_routing.cc: gurka test verifying that perimeter edges are not generated and that routing correctly goes around the area (at the moment, in the future, is expected to generate edges across the area). And 2 more tests, checking that the config option is or not marking the pedestrian areas ways with the area_bit

## Results

Tested on Murcia, Spain extract:

- All 42 multipolygon pedestrian areas are detected, and I have checked manually the member way counts are correct 
- The areas that are simply mapped as ways are also detected and marked
- Gurka test passes: area perimeter generates no edges, route goes around correctly
- With pedestrian_areas: false (default), no behavior change for existing users

items.title: Misinterpretation of highway=pedestrian oneway=yes
items.body:
Valhalla won't route pedestrians against the flow of traffic in a pedestrian area (highway=pedestrian) that's been tagged oneway=yes. Or at least that's what I think is going on in this [example](https://valhalla.openstreetmap.de/directions?profile=pedestrian&wps=-3.205926418304444%2C55.950971946800266%2C-3.205668926239014%2C55.95125729879664).

Is this intentional? I think it's likely to be a misinterpretation of the oneway=yes tag which is [only intended to apply to vehicles](https://community.openstreetmap.org/t/effect-of-oneway-on-pedestrians/7631/19).

For comparison, OSRM and GraphHopper have no problems with sending pedestrians the "wrong way down a one way street."

items.title: Bicycle routing should default to dismount access on footways/pedestrian highways, currently excluded
items.body: Valhalla currently avoids routing bicycles over `highway=footway` and `highway=pedestrian` unless these ways have tags such as `bicycle=dismount`, `bicycle=yes`, `bicycle=permissive`, etc. The router should assume that pushing a bike is generally legal in most footpaths at walking speed, so these ways would still be somewhat strongly avoided unless when they're useful shortcuts. Only `bicycle=no` should be treated as strict prohibition even for pushing.

items.title: feat(mjolnir): allow bicycles on footways/pedestrian ways at walking pace
items.body:
# Issue

Bicycles can currently be routed across a wide range of ways, from bike paths to (in the US) normal paths and steps. But currently they'll never be asked to take a short walk across a crossing or sidewalk even if it's the best way.

Make footways and pedestrian ways routable by defaulting to the equivalent of bicycle=dismount. This has a 2x cost by default but is configurable via `dismount_factor` and `bicycle_dismount_on_pedestrian_ways`.

items.title: fix(sif): apply `walkway_factor` to more pedestrian related uses
items.body: We have `Use`s that we were previously not applying any specific factor to, so they were treated like any other use. I think we can just re-use the more broad `walkway_factor` here. Unfortunately we currently don't have any way to distinguish crossing types (see #6094), nor do we have  a `NodeType` for pedestrian crossings (most pedestrian crossings are mapped as nodes).

items.body:
http://www.openstreetmap.org/directions?engine=mapzen_foot&route=51.2754%2C-1.0684%3B51.2677%2C-1.0882#map=16/51.2715/-1.0783 

http://localhost:8002/route?json={"locations":[{"options":{"allowUTurn":false},"latLng":{"lat":51.26766141261736,"lng":-1.0883197188377378},"_initHooksCalled":true,"lat":51.26766141261736,"lon":-1.0883197188377378},{"options":{"allowUTurn":false},"latLng":{"lat":51.275501353508055,"lng":-1.0679402947425842},"_initHooksCalled":true,"lat":51.275501353508055,"lon":-1.0679402947425842}],"costing":"pedestrian","directions_options":{"language":"en-US"}}

Support issue comments:
"The problem is, this bit of Gresley Road doesn't have a sidewalk: Now, technically people can walk down there (it's not restricted) but it's dangerous, and the intent is that you use the nearby footpath to walk across the bridge and south of the railway line" 

Valhalla only slightly favors a sidewalk compared to a road surface (since not a lot of OSM regions have sidewalk data). This route also suffers from "maneuver penalties" that keep it from going between different named ways. Disable the standard maneuver penalty allows the path to take the bridge pathway. Also, some of the ways in this area are cycleway - which we treat the same as a road (as compared to a footway which would be more heavily favored). We do need to go through an iteration of pedestrian routing updates and this represents a good test case.
